title: Grill — collapse / expand the task messages backlog
summary:
Before this goes to planning: **8 decisions** the build would otherwise make silently, plus six low-stakes defaults I'd bet on. Start with the **surface** and **how the tray opens** — those two change the shape of the plan. The confirm list at the end is one click each.

Source: the Agetor task prompt, quoted verbatim in `docs/plans/messages-backlog-collapse-investigation.md:12-14`. Investigation: `docs/plans/messages-backlog-collapse-investigation.md`.

proven.text: **The surface is the saved-drafts tray, not the kanban column.** The tray is the only UI called “Backlog” that holds saved messages; the kanban `backlog` column holds task cards. `BacklogTray` is rendered at `RunPanel.tsx:4583-4605`.

evidence.label: the tray's header and list
evidence.code: Backlog {items.length} ...

proven.text: **Collapse reclaims ~160 px, not an unbounded list.** The tray is `shrink-0`; the transcript above it is `flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, so hidden tray height goes straight back to the message stream. The list is already capped at 160 px (288 px while editing), plus a ~28 px header.

evidence.label: transcript scroller
evidence.code: className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden p-3 text-xs leading-relaxed [overflow-anchor:none]"

proven.text: **No backend, database, API or CLI change is needed.** `task.backlog` is a JSON column (`Task.backlog` at `src/shared/types.ts:1813`); collapse is pure view chrome. The existing routes all return the full updated `Task` and remain untouched.

**The tray is keyed per task and local state is wiped on remount.** `BacklogTray` is keyed `backlog-${task.id}`; switching task, switching to a subagent tab (the tray unmounts) or closing/reopening the panel (the body unmounts after the exit animation) resets anything held in local `useState`.

**Existing e2e pins today's default-expanded behavior.** The task-switch regression seeds one draft and asserts it is visible without expanding anything; default-collapsed (or an auto threshold of 1) would fail it and force a test change.

evidence.label: the assertion
evidence.code: await expect(panel.getByText("draft that mounts the backlog tray")).toBeVisible();

proven.text: **The house pattern for a disclosure is a hand-rolled full-width button with `aria-expanded` and a chevron; there is no Collapsible primitive, and layout-chrome state lives in `localStorage`.** `panel-collapse.ts` already wraps storage access and reads lazily during first render.

evidence.label: the existing disclosure
evidence.code:
<button
  type="button"
  onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}
  aria-expanded={open}
  className="flex w-full items-center gap-1.5 px-2 py-1 text-left ..."
>
  <ChevronRight className={cn("size-3 shrink-0 transition-transform", open && "rotate-90")} aria-hidden />
  Compaction summary

evidence.label: guarded localStorage helper

proven.text: **New drafts go on top.** `backlog.add` prepends, so a collapsed-header preview or an “expand to see what you saved” action would show the newest draft first.

evidence.label: newest first

sections.title: Surface and default state
sections.intro: These two decide what the plan is building and what every task looks like when opened.

questions.title: Which “backlog” should collapse?
questions.why: This picks the component and decides whether this is a one-component UI change or a different feature.
questions.context: The task details panel has one saved-messages list: the **Backlog** tray directly above the composer. The kanban board also has a column called `backlog`, but it holds task cards, not saved messages; nothing in it can be “saved for later”. The prompt's wording (“we save many messages for later”) matches the tray.

evidence.label: the tray
evidence.code: Backlog {items.length}

evidence.label: the kanban column of the same name

options.label: The saved-drafts tray above the composer
options.description: `BacklogTray` in `RunPanel.tsx` — the only UI that holds saved messages.
options.consequence: One component, UI-only; no API, DB or CLI change.

options.label: The kanban `backlog` column
options.description: The board column of task cards (`ColumnId = "backlog"`).
options.consequence: A different feature: column collapse, unrelated to saved messages.

options.label: Both surfaces
options.description: Add collapse to the tray and the kanban column.
options.consequence: Two features in one plan; the surface and test work roughly doubles.

recommendation.reason: The prompt is about saved messages, and the tray is the only UI that stores them.

questions.title: What state should the tray open in?
questions.why: This decides what every task looks like on open and whether the existing regression test must change.
questions.context: Today the tray is always expanded: a ~28 px header plus a list capped at 160 px — roughly 190–200 px of an 800 px panel. The existing regression test opens a task with one seeded draft and expects it visible (`e2e/task-switch-during-restore.spec.ts:435`), so default-collapsed would require changing that test.

options.label: Expanded, always
options.description: Opens exactly as it does today; only your click collapses it.
options.consequence: Preserves current behavior and the existing test. The big tray is still there until you collapse it once (and the choice can persist — next questions).

options.label: Collapsed, always
options.description: Opens as a header-only bar; you click to reveal the list.
options.consequence: Maximum reading area on every open, but drafts are hidden by default and the existing e2e must expand first.

options.label: Collapsed only when it gets big
options.description: Expanded for a short list, collapsed once it holds at least N drafts.
options.consequence: Directly targets the complaint; needs a threshold (next question) and a precedence rule for a stored manual choice.

recommendation.reason: The request is for an option to reclaim space, not for hiding drafts by default; this also keeps the existing regression test honest.

questions.title: At how many saved messages should the tray auto-collapse?
questions.why: Defines “big” and the exact number the implementation and e2e use.
questions.context: A one-line draft row is roughly 28–32 px, so the 160 px list cap holds about five rows; five is where the tray starts taking its full ~190 px. A manual toggle (remembered per the persistence question) wins over this threshold once stored — the threshold only decides the first open when there is no stored choice.

recommendation.reason: Five rows is where the list reaches its 160 px cap, so it is the first count that actually costs the full slice of the panel.

sections.title: State lifetime and interference
sections.intro: These decide whether the choice sticks, and what happens when the tray changes while you are reading or editing.

questions.title: How long should your collapse choice be remembered?
questions.why: This decides the state owner (tray vs parent), whether a storage key is added, and how many lifecycle tests the plan needs.
questions.context: `BacklogTray` is keyed `backlog-${task.id}`, so local state is wiped on a task switch, a subagent-tab switch (the tray unmounts) and a panel close (the body unmounts after the exit animation) — `RunPanel.tsx:4583-4593`. Layout-chrome state is kept in `localStorage` via `panel-collapse.ts` (guarded read/write, lazy first render), not the server preferences API (`CLAUDE.md:175`).

options.label: Not persisted — session only
options.description: A plain `useState` in the tray; resets on task switch, subagent tab, panel close and restart.
options.consequence: Least code, matches the PR-diff precedent. You re-collapse each time — likely the exact annoyance this feature is meant to remove.

options.label: One global localStorage flag
options.description: `agetor:backlogTrayCollapsed`; the same choice applies to every task and survives restart.
options.consequence: Set once; one key; reuses `readCollapsed`/`writeCollapsed` and its tests. Any task with drafts opens as a collapsed header.

options.label: Per-task localStorage flag
options.description: The key includes the task id, so each task remembers its own state.
options.consequence: Most precise per task, but unbounded keys, a cleanup story, and a key-builder helper plus tests.

recommendation.reason: The complaint is recurring screen occupation; one remembered reading preference is the least code for the best payoff, and `panel-collapse.ts` already solves the storage guards and first-paint.

questions.title: What happens if you collapse while a saved message is being edited inline?
questions.why: The inline editor holds unsaved text in row-local state; this decides whether collapse can lose it and whether the list can be unmounted.
questions.context: The inline editor holds unsaved `draft`/`draftRefs` in `BacklogItemRow` local state (`RunPanel.tsx:5087-5114`); unmounting the list discards them. Keeping the list mounted but hidden preserves the text, but an open `@` popover keeps `data-popover-open` in the DOM (`AtFileAutocomplete.tsx:369`), and `RunPanel`'s Escape handlers bail on that marker (`RunPanel.tsx:544,2258`) — the panel and search can get stuck until the popover is dismissed.

evidence.label: Escape yields to any popover marker

options.label: Block collapse while editing
options.description: The toggle is disabled (or `aria-disabled`) with a hint such as “Save or cancel your edit first”.
options.consequence: No data loss and no hidden-editor trap; because `editingId` is null, the list can safely unmount when collapsed. One click is unavailable in a rare moment.

options.label: Allow collapse; keep the editor mounted but hidden
options.description: The header shows an “editing” cue; expanding restores the unsaved text.
options.consequence: Preserves the draft, but needs explicit blur/popover-close work on collapse to avoid the Escape trap; more code and a new test.

options.label: Collapse saves the edit first
options.description: Clicking collapse runs the existing save path, then closes the editor and collapses on success.
options.consequence: Never loses text; a validation or network failure must keep the tray expanded and show the error.

options.label: Collapse cancels the edit and discards unsaved text
options.description: The tray closes and the edit is thrown away.
options.consequence: Silent data loss; not recommended.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option with no data-loss path and no hidden-focus/popover trap, and the moment is rare enough that blocking one click is cheap.

questions.title: When a new draft is saved while the tray is collapsed, should it expand?
questions.why: This decides whether the parent must control the state and whether there is an expand signal from three save paths.
questions.context: Three paths add drafts: “Save for later” / Enter in this panel (`RunPanel.tsx:3416`), DiffDialog's “Save to backlog” (`DiffDialog.tsx:637-647`), and a server re-stash after a withheld/failed send, surfaced by `send-failed` plus a toast (`App.tsx:1700-1712`). New drafts are inserted at the top (`db.ts:1728-1730`).

evidence.label: Save for later
DiffDialog save

options.label: Stay collapsed; update the count
options.description: The only feedback for a manual save is the count badge; the existing send-failed toast still explains a failed send.
options.consequence: Reading is never interrupted; a manual save is less visually confirmed, but the count is in the header right above the composer.

options.label: Expand on “Save for later” only
options.description: DiffDialog saves and background re-stashes stay collapsed.
options.consequence: Immediate confirmation of the draft you just saved; one deliberate exception to the stored preference.

options.label: Expand on any save you initiate
options.description: Both “Save for later” and DiffDialog's “Save to backlog”; background re-stashes stay collapsed.
options.consequence: Every deliberate save is visible; two paths must feed one expand signal.

options.label: Expand on every addition
options.description: Including the server re-stash.
options.consequence: Nothing is ever added unseen, but the tray can pop open while you are reading.

recommendation.reason: Auto-expanding is the exact interruption the collapse is meant to stop; the count badge stays visible, and the failure path already has its own toast.

sections.title: What collapsed and expanded look like
sections.intro: These decide how much of the header survives and what “expand” means.

questions.title: What should the collapsed header show?
questions.why: This decides the header markup, the copy and whether the collapsed row grows a line.
questions.context: The header currently holds a clipboard icon, “Backlog”, a count badge and a hint: `saved messages — send when you're ready`, or the archived variant `saved messages — unarchive the task to edit or send` (`RunPanel.tsx:5004-5012`). At the 420 px minimum panel width the row fits with room to spare; a leading chevron adds ~18 px. The newest draft is first (`db.ts:1728-1730`), so a preview would show the newest one.

options.label: Keep the current header, add a chevron
options.description: Icon, label, count and the existing hint in both states.
options.consequence: Smallest diff; the chevron is the only new affordance.

options.label: Keep it, but swap the hint when collapsed
options.description: Collapsed: `saved messages — expand to review`; expanded: the current hint.
options.consequence: Tells a first-time user how to get the list back; one conditional string, no extra height.

options.label: Compact: icon, label and count only
options.description: Drop the hint while collapsed.
options.consequence: Least clutter; loses the explanation of what the count is.

options.label: Compact plus a one-line newest-draft preview
options.description: A truncated `line-clamp-1` preview under the header.
options.consequence: Keeps context while collapsed; adds ~16 px and a truncation rule at narrow widths.

recommendation.reason: The chevron alone is standard but easy to miss; explicit copy costs no height and makes the return path obvious.

questions.title: Does “expand” mean the current capped list, or show more?
questions.why: “Expand” could reasonably mean “show all drafts”; that would change the height rule and the transcript reclaim.
questions.context: The list is capped at `max-h-40` (160 px) at rest and `max-h-72` (288 px) while editing; the taller edit cap exists so the Save/Cancel row is not clipped (`docs/plans/fix-backlog-edit-save-button-clipped.md:15-36`). The tray scrolls inside its cap, so even a 30-draft backlog only shows the first few rows today.

options.label: Keep 160 px / 288 px while editing
options.description: Expanding restores exactly today's view.
options.consequence: No layout risk; the transcript reclaim is the only change.

options.label: Make the expanded list taller (e.g. 50–60% of the panel)
options.description: A larger fixed cap, or a viewport-relative one.
options.consequence: You see more drafts at once, but it re-occupies the reading area you just reclaimed.

options.label: Expand shows all drafts (no cap)
options.description: The list grows to fit every item.
options.consequence: Recreates the original complaint on a big backlog; the transcript shrinks instead of grows.

recommendation.reason: The ask is to give the transcript room, not to see more drafts; the 288 px edit cap is a recent fix for clipped Save/Cancel buttons.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Low-stakes defaults I'd bet on. Confirm with one click, or override with what it should be.

recommendation.value: Whole header is one full-width `<button>` with a leading chevron; `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`; `data-testid` hooks (`backlog-tray`, `backlog-toggle`, `backlog-list`) and `data-state`; no height animation, only the chevron rotates.
recommendation.reason: Matches the house disclosure pattern (`CompactionSummaryBlock.tsx:42-57`, `PullCommits`) and gives the e2e stable hooks.

questions.title: Show the collapse toggle for every non-empty tray, even with one draft

recommendation.value: Yes — always show it when the tray renders.
recommendation.reason: A control that appears only past a count is more surprising than a consistent header, and the tray already unmounts when empty.

recommendation.value: Yes — collapse is pure view state; drafts stay visible when expanded and the read-only hint remains.
recommendation.reason: Hiding the list does not mutate the frozen task; the server's `backlogGuard` is untouched.

recommendation.value: Subagent tabs still hide the tray entirely; an empty backlog still hides it; after the last draft is sent or deleted, a later draft follows the stored choice (collapsed if you last collapsed).
recommendation.reason: No new mount gates; the keyed tray already resets local state, and persisted state makes the return state predictable.

recommendation.value: Per-message collapse, expand-all/collapse-all, virtualization for huge lists, backend/preference sync, a Settings toggle, and a new keyboard shortcut.
recommendation.reason: Each is an adjacent feature; adding them would make this a different ticket.

recommendation.value: One new Playwright spec (default visibility, toggle + `aria-expanded`, list hidden, count visible, transcript grows) plus an update to `docs/architecture/messages-backlog.md`; add `CLAUDE.md:175` only if a new localStorage key is introduced. The existing task-switch spec changes only if the chosen default hides its seeded draft.
recommendation.reason: There is no DOM/component harness; e2e is the only layer that can see the disclosure and the reclaimed height.
